Planned.Desc.BootRecovery: Boot repair, EFI and boot-entry management, and Lasteast Rescue Boot media (USB/ISO) based on properly licensed Windows PE.
Planned.Desc.Cleanup: Find temporary and unnecessary files; you choose what is removed, with Recycle Bin support.
Planned.Desc.DiskClone: Clone disks and partitions (intelligent or sector-by-sector) with compatibility checks and verification.
Planned.Desc.DiskConversion: MBR ↔ GPT, FAT32 ↔ NTFS and basic ↔ dynamic conversions, each clearly marked with its data-loss risk.
Planned.Desc.DiskHealth: SMART and NVMe health, temperature and wear monitoring with configurable alerts.
Planned.Desc.FileOperations: Browse partitions, copy and move files, and find files that prevent a partition from shrinking.
Planned.Desc.OsMigration: Move Windows to a new SSD or HDD, preserving boot configuration, with post-migration verification.
Planned.Desc.PartitionManagement: Create, delete, format, resize, move, merge and split partitions through a validated operation queue.
Planned.Desc.PartitionRecovery: Quick and deep scans for lost or deleted partitions, with previews. Recovered data is never written to the source disk.
Planned.Desc.PerformanceLab: Sequential and random benchmarks, surface scan and latency monitoring. Write tests are explained before they run.
Planned.Desc.SmartFix: Scan the computer, explain storage problems by severity, and offer previewed, confirmed fixes.
Planned.Desc.StorageAnalyzer: Treemap of disk usage by folder and file type, with large, old and duplicate file finders.
Planned.Desc.Technician: Disk inventory reports (PDF/CSV/HTML), batch workflows, portable mode and a command-line interface.
Planned.Desc.Tools: Partition table viewer, hex viewer, alignment checker, file system checker and secure wipe.
Planned.Desc.VirtualDisks: Create, attach, expand and compact VHD/VHDX files, clearly separated from the host disk.
Planned.Note: This module is not available in this build. Nothing on this page reads from or writes to your disks.

SF.Align.Explain: Misaligned partitions make SSDs and Advanced Format disks do extra work on every write.
SF.Align.Fix: Alignment requires moving the partition, which comes with the move engine (Phase 5).
SF.Align.Title: Disk {0}, partition {1} is not aligned
SF.AlignOk.Title: All partitions are aligned
SF.C.Blocked: C: cannot grow yet: the {0} partition sits right after it. {1} of free space exists elsewhere on the disk, but using it requires moving that partition, which arrives with the partition-move engine (Phase 5).
SF.C.CanExpand: {0} of unallocated space follows C: directly. C: can grow to {1} without moving any partition.
SF.C.NoFree: There is no unallocated space on this disk. Free space with Cleanup and the Storage Analyzer, or shrink another partition and move it (Phase 5).
SF.C.NotEditable: The Windows disk cannot be changed by Lasteast (dynamic or unsupported layout).
SF.C.NotFound: The Windows volume was not found.
SF.C.NotResizable: The Windows volume's file system cannot be resized by Windows.
SF.C.Title: C: drive
SF.C.Unreadable: The Windows volume could not be read.
SF.CLow.Explain: Windows needs free space for updates, the page file and temporary files. A nearly full system drive slows the PC down and can make updates fail.
SF.CLow.FixExtend: Expand C: into the {0} of unallocated space right after it.
SF.CLow.FixOther: Free up space on the Cleanup page and with the Storage Analyzer, or see the C: drive card above for expansion options.
SF.CLow.Title: C: is running out of space ({0} free)
SF.COk.Title: C: has enough free space ({0})
SF.Dynamic.Explain: Dynamic disks are deprecated by Microsoft. Lasteast shows them read-only; conversion to basic arrives in Phase 5.
SF.Dynamic.Title: Disk {0} is a dynamic disk
SF.EspMissing.Explain: This PC boots in UEFI mode but no EFI system partition was detected. Booting may depend on another disk.
SF.EspMissing.Fix: Do not remove other disks until this is checked. The EFI manager (Phase 8) will inspect it.
SF.EspMissing.Title: No EFI system partition found
SF.EspOk.Title: UEFI boot with an EFI system partition
SF.Footer: Smart Fix never changes anything by itself. "Fix now" adds operations to Pending Operations, where you see the before/after layout and confirm.
SF.Health.Explain: Lasteast does not guess disk health. SMART and NVMe health reading arrives in Phase 9.
SF.Health.Title: Disk health (SMART) not measured yet
SF.Hiber.Explain: If you never use hibernation, this space can be reclaimed. Fast startup also relies on it.
SF.Hiber.Fix: Only if you don't need hibernation or fast startup: run "powercfg /h off" in an administrator prompt.
SF.Hiber.Title: The hibernation file uses {0} on C:
SF.IntroBody: The scan only reads: disks, partitions, free space, alignment, boot layout and temporary files. Every fix is shown to you first and only runs after you confirm it.
SF.IntroTitle: Find out what's slowing down or filling up your storage
SF.Layout.Explain: Partitions overlap or extend past the end of the disk. Writing to this disk could cause data loss.
SF.Layout.Fix: Back up the data on this disk first. Lasteast will not modify it. Partition recovery (Phase 7) can analyse it further.
SF.Layout.Title: Disk {0}: the partition table is inconsistent
SF.LayoutOk.Title: Partition tables are consistent on all {0} disk(s)
SF.Low.Explain: Very full volumes fragment more and leave no room for new files.
SF.Low.Fix: Find large and duplicate files with the Storage Analyzer.
SF.Low.Title: {0} is almost full ({1} free)
SF.Mbr2TB.Explain: MBR can only address the first 2 TB of a disk.
SF.Mbr2TB.Fix: Convert the disk to GPT (disk conversion, Phase 5).
SF.Mbr2TB.Title: Disk {0} wastes {1} because it uses MBR
SF.NoRecovery.Explain: Windows Recovery may still be available from inside the Windows partition; this could not be confirmed without administrator rights.
SF.NoRecovery.Fix: Create rescue media so you can still repair the PC if Windows won't start (Phase 8).
SF.NoRecovery.Title: No recovery partition on the Windows disk
SF.NotElevated.Explain: Scanning works, but applying fixes needs administrator rights.
SF.NotElevated.Fix: Restart Lasteast as administrator before applying fixes.
SF.NotElevated.Title: Lasteast is running without administrator rights
SF.RecoveryOk.Title: Recovery partition present
SF.Recycle.Explain: Deleted files still take space until the Recycle Bin is emptied.
SF.Recycle.Fix: Check its contents and empty it from the desktop when you're sure.
SF.Recycle.Title: The Recycle Bin holds {0}
SF.SpaceOk.Title: Other volumes have enough free space
SF.Subtitle: Scan → understand the problems → recommended fixes → preview → confirm → apply → verify
SF.Summary: {0} item(s) to look at · {1} check(s) passed · scanned at {2}
SF.Temp.Explain: Measured in your user Temp folder and the Windows Temp folder. Programs usually don't need these files after they close.
SF.Temp.Fix: Review and remove them on the Cleanup page.
SF.Temp.Title: {0} of temporary files
SF.Trim.Explain: Without TRIM, SSDs slow down and wear faster over time.
SF.Trim.Fix: In an administrator prompt run: fsutil behavior set DisableDeleteNotify 0
SF.Trim.Title: TRIM is off for SSD disk {0}
SF.Unalloc.Explain: This space is not part of any partition, so Windows cannot use it.
SF.Unalloc.FixCreate: Create a new NTFS partition in it.
SF.Unalloc.FixExtend: Add it to {0}, which ends right where the free space begins.
SF.Unalloc.FixManual: Use "Create partition" on the Overview page to choose size and letter yourself.
SF.Unalloc.Title: {0} of unallocated space on disk {1}
SF.Unreadable.Explain: The volume is locked (BitLocker), has a damaged or unknown file system, or has no media.
SF.Unreadable.Fix: If it is BitLocker-protected, unlock it in File Explorer. Otherwise run "chkdsk X: /f" from an administrator prompt (replace X with the letter). Do not format it if it holds data.
SF.Unreadable.Title: {0} cannot be read
